title: Google Search JSON API alternative: how to replace Custom Search before January 1, 2027
summary: Google's Custom Search JSON API shuts down January 1, 2027. Compare the main replacements on price and output, plus a tested migration to Firecrawl /search.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR**


- Google's Custom Search JSON API has been closed to new customers since January 20, 2026, and stops working for existing customers on **January 1, 2027** .
- The old limits were tight: 100 free queries a day, **$5 per 1,000** after that, a 10,000-a-day cap, 10 results per request and 100 results per query at most.
- Google's own path covers up to **50 domains** through Vertex AI Search (now being renamed Agent Search), whose Enterprise edition, the one website search needs, costs $4 per 1,000 queries. Full web search goes through an interest form with no public price.
- Replacements split two ways: SERP APIs that return Google's result page as JSON, and search APIs built for AI agents that return sources and page content.
- On the independent[OpenBenchmarks web search benchmark](https://openbenchmarks.com/web-search) (last measured October 21, 2026), Firecrawl /search answered **95.3%** of 300 factual lookup questions with a **510 ms** average search time.
- On the same benchmark's hard retrieval task, Firecrawl /search was the **most token-efficient** search-only API, at a median **7,456 tokens** per task.
- Firecrawl also runs its own curated indexes (Research, Developer and Government) and Firecrawl Alexandria, which reaches official data providers across 23 categories. The Custom Search JSON API only ever returned titles, links, snippets and page metadata from Google's index.


---


Google's Custom Search JSON API stops working on January 1, 2027. Teams that still call it have about ten weeks to move.


Google's suggested replacements cover narrower ground than the API did, so most teams need a third-party **Google Search JSON API alternative** . Below are the main options with list prices checked on October 23, 2026, and a tested migration of a` cse.list` call to[Firecrawl /search](https://www.firecrawl.dev/search) that keeps the code around it unchanged.


## What is happening to Google's Custom Search JSON API?


Google's Custom Search JSON API, the REST endpoint behind Programmable Search Engine, is closed to new customers and will be discontinued on January 1, 2027. Existing customers can keep calling it until then at the current price. Search engines created after January 20, 2026 also can't use the "Search the entire web" setting.


Google's Programmable Search Engine team[posted the announcement](https://programmablesearchengine.googleblog.com/2026/01/updates-to-our-web-search-products.html) on January 20, 2026. The[Custom Search JSON API overview](https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/overview) (last updated February 18, 2026) now says the API "is not available for new customers" and that its pricing applies only "until the service discontinuation on January 1, 2027."


Date What changed Source


August 11, 2025 Microsoft retired the Bing Search APIs and pointed customers to Grounding with Bing Search in Azure AI Agents Microsoft Lifecycle announcement


January 20, 2026 Custom Search JSON API closed to new customers; engines created from this date limited to "Sites to search" Google Programmable Search Engine blog


January 1, 2027 Custom Search JSON API discontinued; existing engines lose "Search the entire web" Google blog and API overview


The closure already shows up as errors. Projects that try to start using the API get` 403 PERMISSION_DENIED` and the error text "This project does not have the access to Custom Search JSON API." In July 2026, a Google community manager confirmed in the[Programmable Search help forum](https://support.google.com/programmable-search/thread/411852630/requests-to-google-custom-search-api-fail-with-403-this-project-does-not-have-the-access-to-custom?hl=en) that any search engine created after January 20, 2026 cannot use the API. By October 23, 2026, 146 people had marked[that thread](https://support.google.com/programmable-search/thread/411852630/requests-to-google-custom-search-api-fail-with-403-this-project-does-not-have-the-access-to-custom?hl=en) "I have the same question."


### What were the Custom Search JSON API limits?


The Custom Search JSON API returns at most 10 results per request and never more than 100 results for a single query, according to Google's[cse.list reference](https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/reference/rest/v1/cse/list) . Existing customers get 100 free queries a day, then pay $5 per 1,000 queries up to 10,000 queries a day.


The limits shaped how teams used the API. A request returns a title, link, snippet and some page metadata for each result, so any app that needed the page itself had to fetch and clean every URL in a second step. Reading the top 30 results took three paged calls, and anything past result 100 was out of reach.


## What does Google offer instead of the Custom Search JSON API?


Google offers three paths, and none of them is a drop-in replacement for full web search over JSON. Site search on up to 50 domains moves to the free Programmable Search Element or to Vertex AI Search. Full web search goes through an interest form for a separate product whose price and terms are not public.


- **Programmable Search Element, "Sites to search."** The embeddable search box stays free for engines that list 50 domains or fewer. It runs as a search widget on your web pages.
- **Vertex AI Search, now Agent Search.** Google Cloud's[migration guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/migrate-from-cse) says "Vertex AI Search is being renamed to Agent Search." Website search needs the Enterprise edition, which costs $4.00 per 1,000 queries on[Agent Search pricing](https://cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/pricing) , with 10,000 free trial queries a month. Setup means a Google Cloud project, a data store of URL patterns and an app.
- **Full web search.** Google asks teams that need its whole index to register interest through a form. In September 2026,[Search Engine Watch reported](https://searchenginewatch.com/google-details-partner-only-search-api-as-custom-search-nears-shutdown/) that Google documents a partner-only web search API with no published price or daily allowance. Google has not named it as the Custom Search replacement.


If your app searches a handful of your own domains, Google's path works. If it searches the open web, you need a third-party API.


## What should a Google Search JSON API alternative return?


A Google Search JSON API alternative should return ranked results as JSON with a title, URL and snippet, as Google's list method did. It should also keep the controls you relied on, such as date filters, site filters and country targeting. The bigger choice is whether you need Google's exact result page or the content behind the results.


Five questions sort the options quickly:


1. **Whose results?** SERP APIs fetch and parse Google's own result page. Other APIs return results from their own indexes.
2. **How many results per call?** Google's API stopped at 10. Some replacements return 20 to 100 in one request.
3. **Snippets, pages or source data?** AI agents and retrieval pipelines usually need the page text behind each result, and sometimes the official record behind the page.
4. **How is it billed?** Per request, per credit or per monthly plan, with different free allowances.
5. **How much code changes?** The closer the response shape is to Google's` items` array, the smaller the migration.


## Which Google Search JSON API alternatives are available in 2026?


Firecrawl /search, the Brave Search API, SerpApi and Google's own Agent Search cover most Custom Search use cases in 2026. Prices below are list prices checked on each vendor's own page on October 23, 2026.


Option What it returns Entry list price Free allowance


Firecrawl /search Ranked web, news and image results; optional full-page Markdown per result; Firecrawl's Research, Developer and Government indexes; Firecrawl Alexandria data providers 2 credits per 10 results; Hobby plan $19/month billed monthly (5,000 credits) 1,000 credits a month on the free plan; keyless mode with no API key


Brave Search API Results from Brave's own index; separate LLM context endpoint $5 per 1,000 requests $5 in credits each month


SerpApi Parsed Google result pages and other engines $25/month for 1,000 searches 250 searches a month


Google Agent Search Search over your chosen sites (up to 50 domains on Google's guidance) $4.00 per 1,000 queries (Enterprise edition) 10,000 trial queries a month


The Bing Search API is not on the list because Microsoft[retired it on August 11, 2025](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/announcements/bing-search-api-retirement) . Our[Bing Search API alternatives](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/bing-search-api-alternatives) guide covers that migration.


### How do SERP APIs and search APIs for AI agents differ?


SERP APIs and search APIs for AI agents differ in where results come from. A SERP API returns Google's result page for SEO work. A search API built for AI agents returns results from its own index and favors page content and source data over Google's layout.


**SERP APIs.** SerpApi fetches Google's result page and returns it as JSON, with blocks such as People Also Ask and AI Overviews as separate fields. Pick a SERP API when the exact Google ranking is the data, as in rank tracking.


**Search APIs with their own index.** Firecrawl /search returns ranked results and, in the same call, the full page as Markdown, plus results from Firecrawl's specialized indexes and data providers. Brave Search API serves results from Brave's own index and offers an LLM context endpoint for grounding.


**Google Agent Search.** It suits teams that search their own sites and already run on Google Cloud. It searches only the sites you add to its data store.


## Why use Firecrawl /search to replace the Custom Search JSON API?


Firecrawl /search is a web search API for AI agents that returns ranked results as JSON and, in the same request, the full content of each result as Markdown. It covers the jobs Google's API did, such as date and site filters and country targeting. It also reaches Firecrawl's own curated indexes and official data providers, which the Custom Search JSON API never could.


Firecrawl is the context API for AI agents. The parts that matter for a Custom Search migration:


- **Up to 100 results per request** through` limit` , where` cse.list` capped` num` at 10.
- **Full pages in one call** through` scrapeOptions` , with every option from Firecrawl /scrape available, including Markdown, HTML, links, screenshots and JSON extraction.
- **Filters that map to Custom Search parameters:**` tbs` for time ranges,` includeDomains` and` excludeDomains` for site filters,` country` and` location` for geography.
- **Curated indexes and data providers** through` categories` and Firecrawl Alexandria, covered below.
- **Keyless mode** , so you can test calls with no account or API key, within a daily per-IP limit.


11x, an AI growth platform, uses Firecrawl /search alongside Firecrawl /crawl to research companies for outbound. Its CTO, Jeson Patel, says in the[11x customer story](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/how-11x-automates-prospect-research-with-firecrawl) : "Firecrawl gathers and structures information from across the web to give us a detailed picture of any company."


### How does Firecrawl /search score on independent benchmarks?


On OpenBenchmarks' open-source web search benchmark, Firecrawl /search answered 95.3% of 300 factual lookup questions with a 510 ms average search time. On the hard retrieval task, it was the most token-efficient search-only API, at a median 7,456 tokens per task.


[OpenBenchmarks](https://openbenchmarks.com/web-search) holds the query, the reading model and the judge constant and changes only the search API, with its harness and scoring public on GitHub. The table shows its factual lookup results for the Firecrawl and Brave endpoints it tested, as published on October 21, 2026. SerpApi and Google Agent Search are not on that board.


Search API (endpoint) Accuracy, 300 questions Average search time Average snippet tokens List price per 1,000 queries


Firecrawl /search (` POST /v2/search` ) **95.3%** **510 ms** **678** $5


Brave Search (` /res/v1/web/search` ) 93.3% 630 ms 817 $5


Brave Search (` /res/v1/llm/context` ) 94.0% 601 ms 2,064 $5


Hard retrieval asks an AI agent to find an answer buried in one specific page and passes only with a grounded source URL from that run. On the[token efficiency board](https://openbenchmarks.com/web-search-for-coding-agents/most-token-efficient-search-api) , Firecrawl /search ranks first among search-only APIs at a median 7,456 task tokens with 70.3% task completion. Adding Firecrawl /scrape to fetch full pages lifts task completion to 76.0%, at a median 17,379 tokens. For an AI agent, fewer tokens per answer means lower model cost and more room in the context window.


## How do you migrate from the Custom Search JSON API to Firecrawl /search?


Migrating from the Custom Search JSON API to Firecrawl /search means replacing one GET request with one POST request and renaming a few parameters. If the rest of your code reads each item's title, link and snippet, a small adapter keeps that shape so nothing downstream changes.


The table maps each` cse.list` parameter from Google's reference to its Firecrawl /search equivalent.


Custom Search JSON API Firecrawl /search Notes


` key` (query string)` Authorization: Bearer` header Keyless mode works with no key


` cx` (search engine ID) Not needed Searches the open web by default


` q`` query`` site:` works inside the query


` num` (1 to 10)` limit` (1 to 100) One call replaces paging for most uses


` start` Request` start + num - 1` results and slice Up to 100 results per request


` dateRestrict` (` d1` ,` w1` ,` m6` )` tbs` (` qdr:d` ,` qdr:w` , or a custom` cdr` date range)` sbd:1` sorts by date


` siteSearch` +` siteSearchFilter`` includeDomains` or` excludeDomains` Hostnames only


` gl`` country` (plus` location` ) ISO country code


` searchType=image`` sources: \["images"\]` Also` news`


` fileType=pdf`` categories: \["pdf"\]` Also` research` ,` developer` ,` gov`


Response` items\[\]` Response` data.web\[\]` SDKs return` .web`


` items\[\].link` /` snippet`` url` /` description` Add` markdown` with` scrapeOptions`


The adapter below returns the same` items` fields as` cse.list` and covers the parameters most calls use:` q` ,` start` ,` num` ,` dateRestrict` ,` siteSearch` and` gl` . Call sites switch to its snake_case argument names and drop` cx` ; image and PDF searches map as shown in the table. Install the SDK with` pip install firecrawl-py` .


```text
import   os
from   calendar   import   monthrange
from   datetime   import   date  ,   timedelta
from   urllib  .  parse   import   urlparse


from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl
from   firecrawl  .  v2  .  types   import   ScrapeOptions


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ[  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ])


def   date_restrict_to_tbs  (  date_restrict  ):
unit  ,   count   =   date_restrict  [  0  ],   int  (date_restrict[  1  :]   or   1  )
if   count   ==   1  :
return   f  "qdr:  {  unit  }  "
today   =   date  .  today  ()
if   unit   in   "dw"  :
start   =   today   -   timedelta  (days  =  count   *   (  7   if   unit   ==   "w"   else   1  ))
else  :
years  ,   month   =   divmod  (today.month   -   1   -   count   *   (  12   if   unit   ==   "y"   else   1  ),   12  )
year   =   today  .  year   +   years
start   =   date  (year, month   +   1  ,   min  (today.day,   monthrange  (year, month   +   1  )[  1  ]))
return   f  "cdr:1,cd_min:  {  start  :  %  m  /%  d  /%  Y  }  ,cd_max:  {  today  :  %  m  /%  d  /%  Y  }  "


def   cse_list  (  q  ,   start  =  1  ,   num  =  10  ,   date_restrict  =  None  ,   site_search  =  None  ,
site_search_filter  =  "i"  ,   gl  =  None  ,   full_content  =  False  ):
"""Stands in for cse.list() and returns the same items fields."""
options   =   {  "limit"  :   start   -   1   +   num  }
if   date_restrict  :
options  [  "tbs"  ]   =   date_restrict_to_tbs  (date_restrict)
if   site_search  :
key   =   "include_domains"   if   site_search_filter   ==   "i"   else   "exclude_domains"
options  [  key  ]   =   [site_search]
if   gl  :
options  [  "country"  ]   =   gl  .  upper  ()
if   full_content  :
options  [  "scrape_options"  ]   =   ScrapeOptions  (formats  =  [  "markdown"  ], only_main_content  =  True  )


results   =   firecrawl  .  search  (q,   **  options)
items   =   []
for   hit   in   (results  .  web   or   [])[start   -   1  :  ]  :
url   =   getattr  (hit,   "url"  ,   None  )   or   hit  .  metadata  .  url
item   =   {
"title"  :   getattr  (hit,   "title"  ,   None  )   or   hit  .  metadata  .  title  ,
"link"  :   url  ,
"snippet"  :   getattr  (hit,   "description"  ,   None  )   or   hit  .  metadata  .  description  ,
"displayLink"  :   urlparse  (url).  netloc  ,
}
if   full_content  :
item  [  "content"  ]   =   hit  .  markdown
items  .  append  (item)
return   {  "items"  :   items  }
```


The calling code barely changes. This asks for the second page of results from the past year:


```text
# Before: GET https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1?key=...&cx=...&q=...&num=10&start=11
response   =   cse_list  (  "postgres jsonb index performance"  , num  =  10  , start  =  11  , date_restrict  =  "y1"  )


for   item   in   response  [  "items"  ]  [  :  3  ]  :
print  (item[  "displayLink"  ],   "|"  , item[  "title"  ])
```


Output from our run:


```text
dev.to | PostgreSQL JSONB Indexing: GIN, Expression & Partial Index Strategies
now-next.nl | hstore vs jsonb performance in PostgreSQL, measured - Now-Next
richyen.com | Making JSONB More Queryable with Generated Columns - Richard Yen
```


The adapter also covers site search.` cse_list("pathlib glob", num=3, site_search="docs.python.org")` returned three pages, all from docs.python.org, and` full_content=True` adds each page's Markdown under` content` . Month and year ranges such as` m6` count back by calendar months, as Google's filter does. Billing follows the request: 2 credits per 10 results, plus the scrape cost of each page you fetch (1 credit for a standard page).


If you call the REST API directly, the same request in cURL looks like this:


```text
curl   -s   -X   POST   https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search   \
-H   "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"   \
-H   "Content-Type: application/json"   \
-d   '{
"query": "postgres jsonb index performance",
"limit": 10,
"tbs": "qdr:y",
"country": "US"
}'
```


The response holds ten results under` data.web` , each with` url` ,` title` ,` description` and` position` , and reports` creditsUsed: 2` .


### How do you get full page content with Firecrawl /search?


Firecrawl /search returns full page content when you pass scrape options with the formats you want. Each result then carries its Markdown alongside the title and URL, so an AI agent can read the sources in the same round trip that found them.


The Node.js SDK (` npm install firecrawl` ) takes the same options:


```text
import   { Firecrawl }   from   "firecrawl"  ;


const   firecrawl   =   new   Firecrawl  ({ apiKey  :   process  .  env  .  FIRECRAWL_API_KEY   });


const   results   =   await   firecrawl  .search  (  "kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler example"  ,   {
limit  :   3  ,
scrapeOptions  :   { formats  :   [  "markdown"  ]  ,   onlyMainContent  :   true   }  ,
});


for   (  const   page   of   results  .web   ??   []) {
console  .log  (  page  .  metadata  ?.sourceURL   ??   page  .url  ,   page  .  markdown  ?.  length  );
}
```


Output from our run, with the Markdown length of each page in characters:


```text
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale-walkthrough/ 23875
https://medium.com/@muppedaanvesh/a-hands-on-guide-to-kubernetes-horizontal-vertical-pod-autoscalers-%EF%B8%8F-58903382ef71 26588
https://spacelift.io/blog/kubernetes-hpa-horizontal-pod-autoscaler 20560
```


For page formats beyond Markdown, such as JSON extraction with a schema, see the[Firecrawl /search guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/mastering-firecrawl-search-endpoint) .


## Which curated indexes does Firecrawl /search reach?


Next to its general web search, Firecrawl runs its own curated indexes, including a Research Index of about 43 million paper abstracts, a Developer Index of more than 70 million code sources, and a Government Index of 30 million US government pages. Each one returns primary sources for its domain instead of pages that only mention them.


Index What it covers How to reach it


Web index The live web behind Firecrawl /search, with web, news and image sources Default` sources`


[Research Index](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/research-index-launch) About 43 million paper abstracts from PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv and arXiv, with passage reading and related papers` /search/research` endpoints, such as` /search/research/papers`


[Developer Index](https://www.firecrawl.dev/developer-index) More than 70 million READMEs, issues, merged pull requests, curated documentation sites and OpenAPI specs, most refreshed daily` categories: \["developer"\]` or` /search/developer`


[Government Index](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/government-legal-index) 30 million US government pages: federal and state statutes, regulations, city codes, court opinions and permits` categories: \["gov"\]` or` /search/gov`


A Custom Search engine could restrict results to a list of sites, but it still returned Google's snippets of those pages. An index built for one kind of source returns the paper, the merged pull request or the statute itself, which is what an AI agent needs to cite an answer.


## Can Firecrawl /search find data providers as well as web pages?


Firecrawl /search can return data tools from Firecrawl Alexandria next to web results when you add Alexandria as a source. Firecrawl Alexandria puts official data providers, licensed publishers and Firecrawl's own indexes behind the same API, so an AI agent gets quality data straight from the source instead of a page that describes it.


This is the biggest gap between Firecrawl and the API it replaces. The Custom Search JSON API could only point to pages in Google's index. With Firecrawl Alexandria, a question about a company's filings can go to SEC EDGAR, and a question about an economic series can go to FRED, so the answer comes from the publisher of record. Most search APIs, SERP APIs included, return web results only.

Add` alexandria` to` sources` to see web pages and provider tools in one response:


```text
results   =   firecrawl  .  search  (
"Apple 10-K revenue by segment"  ,
sources  =  [  "web"  ,   "alexandria"  ],
limit  =  3  ,
)


for   hit   in   results  .  web   or   []  :
print  (  "page:"  , hit.url)
for   tool   in   results  .  tools   or   []  :
print  (  "tool:"  , tool.provider, tool.capability)
```


Output from our run (trimmed):


```text
page: https://investor.apple.com/sec-filings/default.aspx
page: https://s2.q4cdn.com/470004039/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/_10-K-2025-As-Filed.pdf

```


Tool discovery is free. Running a tool through Firecrawl /scrape costs that tool's listed credit price.


## Which languages and tools can call Firecrawl /search?


Firecrawl /search is not tied to Python. It has official SDKs in nine languages, a REST API, a CLI, an MCP server for AI assistants and coding agents, and integrations with agent frameworks and no-code tools. Keyless mode lets you try the CLI and MCP server with no API key.


Surface Options


Official SDKs Python, Node.js and TypeScript, Go, Java, Ruby, Rust, .NET, PHP, Elixir


REST API Any language that can send an HTTPS request, as in the cURL example above


[Firecrawl CLI](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli)` npx firecrawl-cli@latest` runs search from a terminal, keyless to start


[MCP server](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server) Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and other AI assistants; keyless at` https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`


Agent frameworks LangChain, LlamaIndex, Mastra, CrewAI, Vercel AI SDK


No-code and workflow tools n8n, Zapier, Make, Dify, Lovable


The SDKs, CLI and REST API share the same endpoints and credit pricing, so a LangChain app that used` GoogleSearchAPIWrapper` can move to Firecrawl in the same framework. For a walkthrough by language, see[how to add web search to an AI app](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/add-web-search-to-ai-app) . If your team needs procurement terms, the[enterprise page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) and[security documentation](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/security) cover them.


## Which Google Search JSON API alternative fits your use case?


The right Google Search JSON API alternative depends on what your app did with Custom Search results. Site search on your own domains fits Google's own path, SEO tools that need Google's exact ranking fit a SERP API, and AI agents that read the pages they find fit Firecrawl /search.


If you used Custom Search for Look at Why


A search box over your own site (50 domains or fewer) Programmable Search Element or Google Agent Search Google keeps supporting site search


Rank tracking and SERP features SerpApi It returns Google's result page as fields


Grounding an LLM or AI agent in live sources Firecrawl /search Results and full-page Markdown in one call


Research pipelines that read many results per query Firecrawl /search Up to 100 results per request, with time and domain filters


Answers that need papers, code, laws or provider data Firecrawl /search with its indexes and Firecrawl Alexandria Primary sources instead of pages that mention them


Search inside a no-code workflow or an AI assistant Firecrawl through n8n, Make, Zapier or the MCP server Same API, no custom code


## What should you do before the Custom Search JSON API shuts down?


Before the Custom Search JSON API shuts down, list every place your code or your vendors call it. Libraries and agent frameworks often wrap the API, so check dependencies as well as your own code, then replace each call behind an adapter and test it on real queries.


1. **Find the calls.** Grep for` googleapis.com/customsearch` ,` cse().list` and wrappers such as LangChain's` GoogleSearchAPIWrapper` .
2. **Write down what each call needs.** Note the result count, filters, and whether a second step fetches the pages.
3. **Pick by job.** Match each call to site search, SERP data or sources for AI agents.
4. **Swap behind an adapter.** Keep the` items` shape so the rest of the code does not change, then delete the second fetch step if your replacement returns page content.
5. **Run both side by side.** Compare results on your real queries while the old API still answers.


Open source projects have started reporting the change. A GitHub issue opened on May 5, 2026 in the OmniRoute project reported that its Google search provider fails for users without prior API access. A Stack Overflow question from June 3, 2026 describes the same 403 on a project with billing active and the API enabled.
